## Finishing

Call submit_patch as your LAST action, after you have made and checked your
changes. Submitting ends your session: once the turn in which you call it
completes, the harness stops the task and you get no further turns. Do not
call it after your first edit and expect to keep working.

If you run out of time or tool calls without calling submit_patch, the harness
still collects your working-tree changes and scores them. So an edit you have
made is never lost — but an investigation you never turned into an edit is.

## Committing to an edit

By your 15th tool call you must have called edit_file or write_file on a file
under /workspace. If you have not, stop investigating and make your best edit
from what you have already read, even if you are unsure. Then keep working:
refine it, check it, and submit at the end.

An empty patch scores zero. A wrong patch also scores zero and costs you
nothing. Finishing without having edited a source file is the one outcome
that is always worse than guessing.

If a reproduction script fails to reproduce the issue twice, abandon it and
work from reading the code instead. Do not rewrite it a third time.

Call get_status to see your remaining time and tool calls. It is free and does
not count against your budget.

## Scratch files

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — anything left in
/workspace becomes part of your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py
or pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading, so editing them
only wastes calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

A truncated result loses information silently, so a broad read wastes a call
and leaves you guessing. Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Use -l to find the file, then -n only within that file. Read with read_file on
a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole file and never cat
one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

        *,
        title: str = "Rich",
        theme: Optional[TerminalTheme] = None,

        font_aspect_ratio: float = 0.61,
        unique_id: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> str:
        """
        Generate an SVG from the console contents (requires record=True in Console constructor).

        Args:
            title (str, optional): The title of the tab in the output image
            theme (TerminalTheme, optional): The ``TerminalTheme`` object to use to style the terminal
            clear (bool, optional): Clear record buffer after exporting. Defaults to ``True``
            code_format (str, optional): Format string used to generate the SVG. Rich will inject a number of variables
                into the string in order to form the final SVG output. The default template used and the variables
                injected by Rich can be found by inspecting the ``console.CONSOLE_SVG_FORMAT`` variable.
            font_aspect_ratio (float, optional): The width to height ratio of the font used in the ``code_format``
                string. Defaults to 0.61, which is the width to height ratio of Fira Code (the default font).
                If you aren't specifying a different font inside ``code_format``, you probably don't need this.
            unique_id (str, optional): unique id that is used as the prefix for various elements (CSS styles, node
                ids). If not set, this defaults to a computed value based on the recorded content.
        """

        from rich.cells import cell_len

        style_cache: Dict[Style, str] = {}

        def get_svg_style(style: Style) -> str:
            """Convert a Style to CSS rules for SVG."""
            if style in style_cache:
                return style_cache[style]
            css_rules = []
            color = (
                _theme.foreground_color
                if (style.color is None or style.color.is_default)
                else style.color.get_truecolor(_theme)
            )
            bgcolor = (
                _theme.background_color
                if (style.bgcolor is None or style.bgcolor.is_default)
                else style.bgcolor.get_truecolor(_theme)
            )
            if style.reverse:
                color, bgcolor = bgcolor, color
            if style.dim:
                color = blend_rgb(color, bgcolor, 0.4)
            css_rules.append(f"fill: {color.hex}")
            if style.bold:
                css_rules.append("font-weight: bold")
            if style.italic:
                css_rules.append("font-style: italic;")
            if style.underline:
                css_rules.append("text-decoration: underline;")
            if style.strike:
                css_rules.append("text-decoration: line-through;")

            css = ";".join(css_rules)
            style_cache[style] = css
            return css

        _theme = theme or SVG_EXPORT_THEME

        width = self.width
        char_height = 20
        char_width = char_height * font_aspect_ratio
        line_height = char_height * 1.22

from rich.console import Console
from rich.style import Style

def test_export_svg_styles():
    console = Console(record=True)
    console.print("Bold", style=Style(bold=True))
    console.print("Italic", style=Style(italic=True))
    console.print("Underline", style=Style(underline=True))
    console.print("Strike", style=Style(strike=True))
    console.print("Bold Italic", style=Style(bold=True, italic=True))
    
    svg = console.export_svg()
    
    # Check for double semicolons
    if ";;" in svg:
        print("Found double semicolons!")
        print(svg)
        return False
    
    print("No double semicolons found.")
    return True

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if test_export_svg_styles():
        print("Test passed!")
    else:
        print("Test failed!")
        exit(1)
